issues.legal_issue: A premises consisting of a building and its appurtenant land must be assessed as a single unit under the method for built premises, while open land without a building is assessed separately under the method applicable to open land.
material_facts: The owner’s premises consisted of a two-storey building and appurtenant land.
The municipal assessment dispute concerned the annual value of the built premises.
The Tribunal determined the annual value by treating the building and appurtenant land as a single unit.
The High Court set aside that determination and directed the Tribunal to assess the building and land separately.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the building and its appurtenant land had to be assessed together under the method applicable to built premises. It allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court’s orders, and restored the Tribunal’s order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 174(1) of the Calcutta Municipal Corporation Act, 1980 governs the annual value of land on which a building is built and requires the building and its appurtenant land to be treated together for determining gross annual rent. Section 174(2) separately governs open land on which no building is built. The two methods operate in separate fields and cannot be combined to assess the same premises. Section 178(2)(i) and (ii) supports treating a building with its site and appurtenant land as a single unit, subject to the specified exceptions. Applying the settled principle that a machinery provision enabling a benefit under a taxing statute is to be construed liberally, the benefit of the interpretation goes to the assessee rather than the taxing authority. The judgment cites G.P. Singh, Principles of Statutory Interpretation, 13th edition, page 856, and relies on no earlier court decision.

predicates.municipal_property_valuation_appeal: An appeal concerns the assessment of the annual value of premises for municipal property taxation.
predicates.premises_contains_building_and_appurtena: The premises being assessed includes a building and land appurtenant to it.
predicates.valuation_concerns_built_premises: The disputed valuation concerns the premises as built, rather than open land on which no building stands.

issues.definition: When a municipal property valuation appeal concerns built premises consisting of a building and appurtenant land, the building and land are assessed together as one unit.
